payload.text: What evidence links open-vocabulary visual features to actionable part-level affordance predictions?
Dataset-grounded affordance labels make interaction regions measurable but narrow vocabulary and scenario coverage.
Dense foundation-model descriptors can expose reusable part correspondences that support affordance transfer.
AGD20K and LOCATE provide public anchors for grounding affordance regions in images.
Dense ViT descriptors and later foundation encoders are public anchors for probing visual correspondence.
If descriptors align semantically similar object parts, they can support affordance transfer across categories.
Demo evidence is intentionally lightweight and should not be treated as reviewed project truth.

node.text: What mechanistic primitives make visual affordance understanding possible in Visual Foundation Models?
Can affordance reasoning in VFMs be explained as composition of geometric perception and interaction perception?
How can we distinguish genuine affordance-relevant cues from object semantics, part segmentation, or prompt-conditioned localization?
Affordance reasoning in VFMs can be decomposed into two composable primitives: geometric perception and interaction perception.
Part-level geometric structure in discriminative and self-supervised VFMs provides the spatial substrate for affordance localization.
Generative VFMs encode interaction priors that associate actions with plausible object contact regions.
Training-free fusion of geometric primitives and interaction priors supports a mechanistic account of affordance reasoning in VFMs.
Across probed VFMs, stronger geometric awareness aligns with better UMD affordance segmentation under controlled linear probing; depth and normal cues improve weaker geometry models.
DINO-family representations expose stable part-level geometric structure; PCA is used as a method tool to isolate compact geometric prototypes.
Flux and Flux Kontext verb-conditioned cross-attention localizes plausible interaction or contact regions and remains meaningful even when generation quality is imperfect.
DINO geometry prototypes combined with Flux interaction maps yield training-free zero-shot affordance masks competitive with weakly supervised methods on AGD20K.
Object-part affordance work shows that affordance prediction depends on localized functional parts rather than object category alone.
Exocentric and interaction-grounded affordance work shows that observed action-object interaction can reveal actionable regions.
Open affordance and language-conditioned grounding work shows the field pressure beyond fixed labels, while also exposing the risk that language semantics alone may not ground contact regions.
Dense descriptor and VFM-prior work shows that frozen visual models can expose dense part or geometry correspondences worth probing.
If affordance is a relation between agent action and object structure, then an account based only on object semantics or part segmentation is incomplete.
If internal visual representations separate functional parts, they can support affordance transfer beyond fixed object categories.
If verb-conditioned generative signals consistently localize contact regions, they can function as interaction priors.
If independently probed geometry and interaction primitives can be composed without task-specific training to produce affordance maps, that supports a mechanistic account.
The mechanistic account depends on the quality of extracted primitives: DINO geometry can be entangled with semantics, and Flux attention can be noisy or unstable.
The evidence shows usable internal signals and composability, but does not fully prove that VFMs causally understand affordance in the human or embodied sense.
UMD and AGD20K provide measurable affordance targets, but their masks or heatmaps only approximate the richer action-object relation.
The training-free fusion is deliberately shallow; it demonstrates composability of primitives, not an optimal or complete affordance reasoning system.
The paper studies visual grounding of affordance, not closed-loop manipulation, physical success, or policy learning.
